failover_workflow.note: T5.2, live-tested 2026-09-03 against a real n8n instance (n8nio/n8n:latest in the data stack) -- not just re-validated as JSON. Along the way, dispatch moved off Execute Command entirely: Run_Failover_Router is now an HTTP Request node calling POST {COCKPIT_URL}/failover/dispatch (new cockpit/app.py route that runs router/failover.py's dispatch_next() in-process), because n8n's official Docker image ships no python3 and has no repo mounted, so `python3 router/failover.py` could never have worked there regardless of ARK_REPO_PATH. Commit_Genome_Update still uses Execute Command (git add/commit/push) and still needs a host where git + a repo checkout are actually available -- that part remains untested live. Discord/Google Sheets nodes (Notify_Dispatch_Success, Alert_No_Backend, Alert_Dispatch_Failed, Log_Idle_Heartbeat) still need real credentials, untested live. Found and fixed 3 more real n8n v2 defaults blocking this while getting the dispatch path working: NODES_EXCLUDE (Execute Command disabled by default), N8N_BLOCK_ENV_ACCESS_IN_NODE (blocks $env.* in expressions), and host.docker.internal not resolving on native Linux Docker without extra_hosts: host-gateway. All three documented inline in docker-compose.yml. Live run result: Failover_Heartbeat -> Run_Failover_Router (real HTTP call, real response) -> Check_Dispatch_Status all executed successfully in n8n, correctly returning/branching on {"status": "no_backend_available", "task_id": "T5.1"} -- the same honest result router/failover.py gives standalone in this sandbox (no API keys, no local Ollama).

cockpit_failover_dispatch_route.note: Added while live-testing T5.2: runs FailoverRouter(state_path=ARK_STATE_PATH).dispatch_next() and returns the result as JSON, so n8n's HTTP Request node (or anything else) can trigger the failover cascade without needing python3/git/a repo checkout in its own runtime. 2 tests in tests/test_cockpit.py::TestFailoverDispatchEndpoint.

control_plane.note: Added directly to this branch on 2026-07-19 by the repo owner (commits 89e0428..5ce3c5b), not via router/failover.py dispatch. ControlPlane registers the 8 existing ARK95X roles (arc_x, codex_security, memory_cortex, monitoring, github, n8n, devices, business_ops) under one authority/reporting contract, with ARK-STATE.json declared as AUTHORITATIVE_STATE_PATH. Agents cannot override the plane or self-approve; financial/legal/public/destructive/deployment/security/system-mutation/account-change actions route to queued_for_human_approval. It does not yet read or write ARK-STATE.json in code -- that's the documented next pass. See docs/control-plane-pass-1.md for the full contract. Verified independently: 65 tests pass repo-wide (13 control_plane tests included), flake8 clean, CI (lint/test/Code Audit Master) green on commit 5ce3c5b.

control_plane_ledger_gate.note: T5.5: the 'next adjustment pass' from docs/control-plane-pass-1.md, wired for real. CommandLedger now takes an optional control_plane; closing a position is a 'financial' action, which control_plane.APPROVAL_REQUIRED_ACTION_CLASSES always routes to queued_for_human_approval. Money does not move until CommandLedger.approve_pending_action() executes it and reports the real outcome back to the control plane via ControlPlane.report(). cockpit/app.py wires this in by default (CONTROL_PLANE_ENABLED=true) -- POST /fills queues, GET /pending shows the queue, POST /approve/{request_id} executes, GET /control-plane exposes the live authority/reporting state. Proved live 2026-09-03: ran uvicorn with the gate on, POSTed a real signal and a real fill request, confirmed /roi stayed at $0 pnl while queued, approved it, confirmed /roi then showed the real $200 P&L, and confirmed business_ops's last_report in /control-plane matched the real ledger_entry.entry_id. Backward compatible: control_plane=None (or CONTROL_PLANE_ENABLED=false) preserves the original immediate-execution behavior, covered by tests.

control_plane_gate_tests.note: 11 tests total: ledger-level (money doesn't move until approved, control plane gets the report, two pending closures stay independent) and cockpit-level (queue/pending/approve/control-plane endpoints).

prove_the_network_script.note: Re-runnable proof: drives the real cockpit app in-process to prove the authority gate blocks and then releases real money with a matching control-plane audit trail, then proves the failover router's cascade (Claude skipped -> Ollama picked up) and its write-back into a scratch genome file. 15/15 checks pass. `python3 scripts/prove_the_network.py`.

data_stack.path: docker-compose.yml (postgres, mongodb, redis, qdrant, n8n services)
data_stack.note: Brought up live 2026-09-03 via `docker compose up -d postgres mongodb redis qdrant n8n` -- all 5 healthy and verified with real commands (pg_isready, redis-cli ping, mongosh ping, qdrant /healthz, n8n /healthz), not just 'container running'. Found and fixed 4 real pre-existing bugs in docker-compose.yml along the way: (1) core service had `env_file: .env` spliced into the middle of its `ports:` list, breaking YAML parsing for the whole file; (2) n8n's DB_POSTGRESDB_DATABASE=n8n was never created by anything (only `sovereign` is, via postgres's POSTGRES_DB) -- n8n crash-looped with 'database n8n does not exist' until the database was created manually; (3) n8n defaults to binding IPv6 `::`, unavailable in network-restricted sandboxes -- added N8N_LISTEN_ADDRESS=0.0.0.0; (4) qdrant's healthcheck used `curl`, which the qdrant/qdrant image does not ship -- replaced with a bash /dev/tcp port probe. app services (core/dashboard/flamegate/comet-router/gate-unlocker/council/shadow-agent) and monitoring (searxng/prometheus/grafana) were left alone -- out of scope for 'data stack' and mostly reference unbuilt/stub application code per MIGRATION_ROADMAP.md.

control_plane_remaining_adapters.path: monitoring/health.py, memory_cortex/proposals.py, codex_security/scanner.py, devices/local_exec.py, github_adapter/repo_state.py, n8n/dispatch_adapter.py, router/failover.py (arc_x wiring) + cockpit/app.py (GET /monitoring/health)
control_plane_remaining_adapters.note: T5.6: all 7 remaining adapters wired into ControlPlane.report()/request_action() at their own real integration points (business_ops/command_ledger from T5.5 was the template; none of these are a generic shim). monitoring: monitoring/health.py's run_health_check() does a real ledger-reachability check plus best-effort TCP probes of the docker-compose data stack's standard ports, reported through control_plane and exposed at GET /monitoring/health (existing /health left untouched so it stays CI-safe). memory_cortex: memory_cortex/proposals.py's MemoryCortexAdapter proposes known_gaps/todo_queue patches via action_class=memory_update (not in APPROVAL_REQUIRED_ACTION_CLASSES, so it auto-queues as queued_for_control_plane) and is the only thing that then actually writes the patch to the state file and reports the real outcome. codex_security: codex_security/scanner.py's CodexSecurityAdapter runs a real regex secret-pattern scan (AWS keys, generic api_key/secret/token assignments, PEM private key headers, Slack/GitHub tokens) over real `git diff --name-only` changed files (or explicit paths); a finding reports status=vetoed, a clean scan still requests release under action_class=security_sensitive (always queued_for_human_approval -- never self-released). devices: devices/local_exec.py's DevicesAdapter does a real, ungated `docker compose ps <service>` status check, and gates `docker compose restart <service>` behind action_class=system_mutation (request_restart queues for human approval; only approve_pending_action() actually runs the subprocess and reports the real returncode/stdout/stderr). github: github_adapter/repo_state.py's GitHubAdapter reports real `git status`/`git log` state (HEAD, branch, dirty file count) directly, and gates a real `git push` behind action_class=deployment (queued for human approval; approve_pending_push() runs it and reports success/failure) -- local-git-based only, no GitHub API credentials assumed. n8n: n8n/dispatch_adapter.py's N8nDispatchAdapter is the code-side mirror of workflows/ark_failover_dispatch_v1.json's Check_Dispatch_Status branches -- a 'dispatched' result requests the genome commit+push as action_class=account_change (queued for human approval, matching invariant 7: n8n is transport, not the brain); no_backend/dispatch_failed report as alerts, no_pending_tasks reports as idle. arc_x: router/failover.py's FailoverRouter now takes an optional control_plane; every dispatch_next() call requests the routing decision as action_class=routing (arc_x's own authority scope, not approval-required, so it proceeds immediately) and reports the outcome (routed/no_backend/dispatch_failed/idle) back through the plane -- this is arc_x's real 'route_agents'/'simulate' job per docs/control-plane-pass-1.md. All 7 are additive and optional (control_plane=None preserves prior behavior everywhere), covered by 50 new tests (tests/test_monitoring_health.py, test_memory_cortex.py, test_codex_security.py, test_devices.py, test_github_adapter.py, test_n8n_dispatch_adapter.py, test_failover_arc_x_control_plane.py, test_cockpit_monitoring_health.py). 130/130 tests pass repo-wide, flake8 clean.

postgres_ledger_backend.path: passive_income_engine.py (postgres_url param, _pg_* methods) + cockpit/app.py (POSTGRES_URL env var)
postgres_ledger_backend.note: PassiveIncomeEngine now takes an optional postgres_url; when set it creates ledger_state (single row: starting_balance/balance/breakeven_cost_usd) and ledger_entries tables in Postgres, restores from them on init (Postgres is authoritative over persist_path when both given), and writes every record_entry() to Postgres in addition to/instead of the JSON file. cockpit/app.py picks POSTGRES_URL over LEDGER_PERSIST_PATH automatically when set. Proved live 2026-09-03 against the real postgres container: ran the full control-plane-gated signal->fills->approve flow through a real uvicorn process, then queried Postgres directly with `docker exec ... psql` (outside the app entirely) and confirmed the exact real ledger_entries row and updated ledger_state.balance. Also proved durability: a brand-new PassiveIncomeEngine instance pointed at the same postgres_url restores the prior state exactly (ignoring the constructor's starting_balance argument), simulating a process restart. tests/test_passive_income_engine_postgres.py (3 tests) skips gracefully when no Postgres is reachable, so this repo's CI (which doesn't run docker-compose) stays green; run `docker compose up -d postgres` first to exercise them. requirements.txt gained psycopg2-binary.

backend_router.note: router/failover.py implements this. FailoverRouter.dispatch_next() reads todo_queue above, finds the first entry with status=pending and all depends_on marked done, and dispatches it to whichever backend's is_available() returns true first, in priority order below.

handoff_protocol.rule: Any model resuming this build reads ARK-STATE.json first, finds the lowest-numbered todo_queue entry with status=pending and satisfied depends_on, executes it, then updates that entry's status plus updated_at/updated_by before stopping. Never merge the working branch's PR to main autonomously -- that is a human decision (see T5.1).
